title: Individual logons on shared terminals
objective: Every action on a shared front desk or back office terminal can be traced to one named person.
requirement: The property shall require an individual logon on every shared terminal and shall use fast user switching so that staff do not share one account across a shift.
rationale: Front desks run round the clock and terminals change hands at every shift change, so shared logons hide who handled a booking or a card.
evidence_expected: Terminal logon configuration screenshot; Account list reconciled to the staff roster
assessment_question: Does every shared terminal require a named logon with fast user switching and is the account list checked against the staff roster?

title: Privileged access for administrators
objective: Administrative rights are held by named people and granted only for a stated need.
requirement: The property or its managing party shall keep a list of privileged accounts across all properties and shall approve each grant of administrative rights in writing.
rationale: Seasonal and outsourced staff move between properties and a single forgotten administrator account can reach several sites.
evidence_expected: Privileged account list; Approval record for administrative rights
assessment_question: Is there a current list of privileged accounts with a written approval for each one?

title: Multi factor authentication for remote, administrative and cloud access
objective: Stolen passwords alone cannot open remote, administrative or cloud hosted systems.
requirement: Multi factor authentication shall protect every remote access path, every administrative logon to servers and every administrator account of a cloud hosted service.
rationale: Hotels depend on vendor remote access and on cloud hosted booking and property systems that are reachable from the internet.
evidence_expected: Multi factor enrolment report; Remote access configuration screenshot
assessment_question: Is multi factor authentication enforced for remote, administrative and cloud administrator logons?

title: Role hardening baselines
objective: Each server and workstation role starts from a documented secure configuration.
requirement: The property shall keep a hardening baseline per system role that covers SMB signing, name resolution fallbacks, network level authentication for remote desktop and legacy services, and shall check systems against it.
rationale: Scans of the case group showed the same weak settings repeated on most systems, which points to missing role baselines.
evidence_expected: Hardening baseline per role; Latest configuration check result
assessment_question: Does a written hardening baseline exist for each system role and was it checked in the last review period?

title: Patch windows that fit round the clock operation
objective: Security updates reach property systems without stopping the front desk.
requirement: The property shall agree patch windows with front office and vendors for every critical system, shall apply critical updates inside an agreed number of days and shall record exceptions.
rationale: A hotel cannot switch off its property management system at will, so patching needs a planned window and a fallback.
evidence_expected: Patch window schedule; Exception register with approvals
assessment_question: Are patch windows agreed for critical systems and are late patches recorded as exceptions?

title: TLS, certificates and cleartext services
objective: Data in transit between hotel systems is protected with current protocols and valid certificates.
requirement: The property shall retire legacy TLS and SSL versions and weak ciphers, shall replace untrusted or self signed certificates on guest and payment facing services and shall remove cleartext services.
rationale: Interface servers and guest facing systems often keep old protocol settings for compatibility with vendor software.
evidence_expected: Protocol and certificate scan result; Certificate inventory with expiry dates
assessment_question: Are legacy protocols, weak ciphers, untrusted certificates and cleartext services removed from systems that carry guest or card data?

title: Card data environment scope per property
objective: The property knows which systems store process or transmit card data.
requirement: The property shall document the card data environment with a system and network diagram and shall review it after every change to payment devices or networks.
rationale: Payment terminals and the property management system often sit on the same flat network so the real scope is wider than assumed.
evidence_expected: Card data flow diagram; Scope review record
assessment_question: Is there a current diagram of the card data environment that was reviewed after the last change?

title: Network separation of POS and payment terminals
objective: A compromise elsewhere on the property network cannot reach payment systems.
requirement: Point of sale systems and payment terminals shall sit in their own network zone with a deny by default rule set toward the rest of the property network.
rationale: A flat hotel network lets a weak workstation reach the systems that handle card data.
evidence_expected: Firewall rule extract for the payment zone; Network diagram showing the zone
assessment_question: Are payment systems in a separate zone with deny by default rules?

title: Card data retention limits and tokens
objective: Card numbers are not kept longer or in more places than the business needs.
requirement: The property shall use tokens instead of card numbers in the property management system where the vendor supports it and shall delete stored card data after the agreed retention period.
rationale: Stored card numbers in old reservations create breach exposure long after the stay has ended.
evidence_expected: Retention schedule for card data; Tokenisation setting in the property management system
assessment_question: Are tokens used in place of card numbers and is stored card data deleted after the retention period?

title: One approved remote access path
objective: All vendor and staff remote access uses one controlled and monitored route.
requirement: The property shall allow remote access only through one approved path and shall remove other remote access tools from every system.
rationale: Scans found several remote access tools on hotel systems, which leaves vendors and attackers more than one way in.
evidence_expected: Approved remote access design; Software inventory showing no unapproved tools
assessment_question: Is there one approved remote access path and have unapproved remote tools been removed?

title: Named vendor accounts with approved time windows
objective: Vendor access exists only for named people and only while work is approved.
requirement: Each vendor user shall have a named account that is enabled for an approved time window and disabled afterwards.
rationale: Vendors support hotel systems from outside and shared vendor accounts leave no record of who acted.
evidence_expected: Vendor account list with owners; Access approval tickets
assessment_question: Do vendor users have named accounts that are enabled only for approved windows?

title: Remote session logging
objective: Vendor sessions can be reviewed after the event.
requirement: The approved remote access path shall record who connected, to which system and for how long, and the property shall keep these logs for the period set in the obligations register.
rationale: After an incident the property needs to show what a vendor did on a building or guest system.
evidence_expected: Remote session log sample; Log retention setting
assessment_question: Are remote sessions logged with user, target and duration and kept for the required period?
